title: Phase-aligned oscillator dependence and independent gradients
observable: Phase alignment index cos(arg(sum_f conj(Fi) * Fj)) over 10-500 uHz (Paper 1 / Step 53).  This is the corrected phase observable that gives lambda ~ 4200 km with R^2 ~ 0.90 and z ~ 27 vs the phase-randomised null on independent products.  Amplitude-based metrics fail because GNSS processing suppresses spatially correlated amplitudes when phases are aligned.
interpretation: The phase alignment index is computed separately for quartz-quartz and atomic-atomic pairs.  If TEP couples to quartz but not atomic (Step 65 screening), quartz pairs should show a clear Gaussian decay at ~4200 km (high R^2, large z vs the phase-randomised null) while atomic pairs should not (low R^2, small z).  The difference is the differential field coupling that conventional physics does not predict: the atomic transition screens the field, so atomic clocks do not develop the phase-coherent spatial structure that quartz clocks do.
